label: Sevoflurane — MAC + partition coefficients

extraction.tier_rationale: MAC anchored at age 40; the universal age-correction (Mapleson/Nickalls, ~6%/decade) is applied by the kernel.
Standard textbook MAC-awake value; clinical value is lowered by opioid co-administration (noted in prose, not the tier).
Textbook physicochemical constant governing speed of onset/offset.

pharmacogenomic_safety_flags.consequence: malignant hyperthermia — a life-threatening hypermetabolic crisis
pharmacogenomic_safety_flags.action: AVOID all volatile agents and succinylcholine in an MH-susceptible patient (use a trigger-free / total-intravenous technique)

extraction.tier_rationale: CPIC guideline-grade gene-trigger link (RYR1/CACNA1S -> MH on volatile or succinylcholine exposure). A SUSCEPTIBILITY, not a kinetic change: rendered as a hard avoidance flag with no dose effect (v0.9 §2 Trap 2).

MAC40 anchor + Mapleson age-correction + textbook partition coefficients. The age-correction relation is the verified, load-bearing equation; the constants are standard. Not compartmental PK — a distinct (physicochemical) parameter convention.

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 4.8 via Hypnos research agents)
source_review.method: fetched open-access reproductions, primary-paper PubMed abstracts, FDA labels, and/or the tci R package source, then numerically compared each curated typical-value parameter against the fetched values (see sources)
source_review.notes: Sevoflurane MAC40 1.8 matches Wikipedia's explicit age-40 baseline (some modern refs cite ~2.0). Blood:gas is SPLIT in the literature: curated 0.65 (anaestheasier) vs 0.69 (StatPearls, GasGasGas) - both circulate; a human should confirm the dataset's convention. oil:gas 47 confirmed (GasGasGas). MAC-awake 0.62 NOT confirmed from a fetched page body (only qualitative ~0.25-0.5 MAC) - human item. Age-MAC exponent corroborated indirectly.

notes: MAC fraction (depth surrogate) = end-tidal% / MAC(age). With nitrous oxide, MAC fractions add (additivity). blood:gas governs onset speed; oil:gas correlates with potency (Meyer-Overton).
